clue.text: Team on board increase knots

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts the team between the letters of the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel boarded
a crew is a team, as of a boat
to up something is to increase it

explanation.surface: A crew aboard ship ramps up its knot speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knots' looks like a speed unit at sea but is a verb meaning tangles or bungles.
explanation.definitionFit: To knot something is to tangle or botch it, the same idea as making a mess of it.

clue.text: Head of laboratory getting paid for knowledge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of laboratory is used

parts.note: earning means getting paid for work

explanation.surface: A lab director is paid for expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is acquired knowledge, a close synonym.

clue.text: Stiffener produced by celebrity chef? Not half!

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: only half of the word chef is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Is a famous cook the source of laundry stiffener? Hardly, says the exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity chef' reads as one phrase, but the two words do separate jobs; 'Not half!' looks like an emphatic 'certainly', yet it keeps only half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is used to stiffen fabric such as collars, so it is a stiffening agent.

clue.text: Flag of British queen and king

parts.note: Anne was a queen of Great Britain
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal standard belonging to a British queen and king.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag or long strip of cloth carried on a pole.

clue.text: Tired out? Completely, everything considered

parts.note: all in is an idiom for exhausted
all can mean wholly, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they are exhausted replies: completely, on balance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning taking everything into account, on the whole.

clue.text: Visit nurse after a time

indicators.note: after places the nurse word behind the a and time pieces

parts.note: to tend someone is to nurse them

explanation.surface: A nurse makes a home visit after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a place or event is to go to it, to visit.

clue.text: Change name in secret

indicators.note: in places the name abbreviation inside the word for secret

parts.note: covert means secret or hidden

explanation.surface: Switching one's name covertly, as a spy might.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert is to change something from one form into another.

clue.text: Depths of drain in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so the letters of drain are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A blocked drain is the lowest point of a bad day.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the depths of a situation.

clue.text: Circular meadow left mowed

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: mowed means cut down and disordered, so the letters of left are scattered

explanation.surface: A notice reports the field was cut on the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective describing the meadow, but it is the noun meaning a handout; 'mowed' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a printed notice handed out widely, as is a leaflet.

clue.text: Cryptic clue fair? Without a match!

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are jumbled
without asks for the letter a to be taken away from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether a cryptic clue is fair when it has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUE plus FAIR minus A leaves CLUEFIR, which rearranges to the answer. 'Without a match' looks like 'unequalled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer was an old name for a friction match.

clue.text: Stop men finding female sorcerer's home

parts.note: an end is a stop or conclusion
OR stands for other ranks, the soldiers

explanation.surface: Halting soldiers who track down a witch's dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the Witch of Endor lived there, so it was a sorceress's home.

clue.text: New doctrine, Eastern, not understood by many

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of doctrine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel Eastern teaching that few people grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure, little known, beyond most people's grasp.

clue.text: Plain sailing? Right on!

definitions.meaning: an easy, uncomplicated course of action

explanation.surface: An easy voyage, cheered with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and easy, and also, split in two, meaning directly ahead.

clue.text: One villain after power in a boat

indicators.note: after puts the one and villain pieces behind the power letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A lone baddie seeks power while sitting in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a long dugout canoe, a kind of small boat.

clue.text: Tenant and I study in peace

indicators.note: in places the I and study pieces inside the word for peace

parts.note: rest is peace and quiet
taken as written
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A lodger studies quietly in their room.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident lives in a place, as a tenant does.

clue.text: See hunt abandoned — wax lyrical?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeing a hunt called off, someone rhapsodises about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax lyrical is to speak with eager delight, to gush.

clue.text: Circle with sawn-off firearm?

indicators.note: a sawn-off gun has its end cut away, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

explanation.surface: Going round in circles with a sawn-off shotgun.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve is to turn or move in a circle.

clue.text: French satirist showing anger after dance

indicators.note: after puts the anger word behind the dance

parts.note: the volta is an old lively dance
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A French satirist gets angry following a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire was the eighteenth-century French writer of Candide, a great satirist.

clue.text: I'm dividing possessions for valuation

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the possessions word by sitting inside it

parts.note: an estate is all of someone's possessions
the letters I and M, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone splits up a dead relative's belongings to have them priced.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate valuation or reckoning of worth.

clue.text: Just as important, like the anchor leg runner in a relay team?

definitions.meaning: a phrase introducing a final item of equal importance

definitions.text: like the anchor leg runner in a relay team?
definitions.meaning: the anchor runs the final leg and is often the strongest runner

explanation.surface: The final relay runner matters just as much as the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom introducing a final item that matters as much as the others.

clue.text: Enjoys duck in this manner

parts.note: likes means enjoys
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of duck prepared in this particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: Like so means in this way, as shown.

clue.text: Dog used in hunting wild beasts

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of beasts run free and rearrange

explanation.surface: A hound is employed to chase wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hound bred for tracking hares by scent.

clue.text: Duty elsewhere on diamonds

parts.note: off means away, gone elsewhere
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A job away from base, dealing in jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a duty or position of responsibility, as in the office of mayor.

clue.text: A profit once more

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Making a profit one more time.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, a second time.

clue.text: A piece of cake children eat gluttonously

parts.note: kids are children
to stuff oneself is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Youngsters greedily wolf down a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for something very easy, a simple task.

clue.text: Warning a member about lake

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club member issues a caution concerning the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a warning signal of danger.

clue.text: Open, following on

parts.note: since means following in time, after
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Something opens after an earlier item.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and frank, an open manner.

clue.text: Small crown made of gold, one shown in court

indicators.note: shown in places the gold and one pieces inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gold tiara displayed at a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles.
